text: job-deliverable-v1 task=ka41a2f6f72 | Setuid-root should not be the default: any parsing, path, fd, or library bug executes with full root authority. If a helper is unavoidable, make the privileged phase tiny: open/rename only pre-approved log targets, then immediately setgid/setuid to a fixed unprivileged account and verify the drop cannot be regained; this limits post-action compromise. Clear the environment and use fixed absolute program/library behavior so PATH, loader, locale, or config variables cannot redirect privileged execution. Close all inherited file descriptors except an explicit allowlist so the caller cannot smuggle privileged sockets/files into the helper. Resolve paths from a trusted directory fd, reject .., require expected owner/type, and use no-follow/exclusive-style opens so symlink or rename races cannot redirect rotation onto arbitrary root files. Prefer a root-owned rotation daemon/socket with a narrow request protocol, or a dedicated group/capability granting only the needed file operation; the tradeoff is extra service/configuration complexity and tighter ACL maintenance. Verdict: do not ship the original broad setuid-root design; redesign around least privilege first.
